Skuodas Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Klaipėdos apskritis, Lithuania

Not demolished. Skuodas's shoe industry produced 400 pairs of shoes a day, marketed throughout Lithuania. Until the end of WWI, the Jewish community was governed by an elected twelve-person committee known as 'The Dozen' (Di Tsvelftlech). The entire Jewish community was annihilated in summer 1941 at four different sites in and around the town; a small number of young people escaped with retreating Red Army troops, though most of them later fell in battle. After the war, Stalinist authorities planned to build a new marketplace on this cemetery's grounds, but a Skuodas Jew appealed directly to Moscow and prevented it — though the tombstones themselves were still carted away for other building projects. On July 10, 1941, members of the local 'Riflemen' militia brought about 20 Jewish men to the cemetery itself and executed them in bomb craters.
